_comment: Three worked examples to show the shape. Milestone 1 is getting this to twenty, with at least four deliberately awkward ones, BEFORE you write a prompt. Invent every one of them: no real supplier, no real person, no real invoice. The verifier checks your scoring script, not this file — the count is on you, and writing eighteen easy examples to make the number look good only fools you.

examples.name: clean and ordinary
examples.input:
HARMATTAN SUPPLIES LTD
Invoice INV-2026-114
Date issued: 4 February 2026
PO: none

2 x Field jacket    48,500.00
Total due: NGN 48,500.00

examples.name: awkward: ambiguous date, two readings
examples.input:
LAGOS CANVAS CO
Inv. 2026/03/04
Issued 03/04/2026
Amount: 27,500.50 NGN
Purchase order 88120
examples.note: 03/04/2026 is 3 April or 4 March depending on where it was written. There is no way to tell from the document, so the only honest answer is null and a low confidence. A model that picks one is guessing, and this example exists to catch that.

examples.name: awkward: total is not the largest number
examples.input:
JOS PLATEAU WOOL
Invoice JP-9
12 Jan 2026

Subtotal      985,000.00
Discount      -98,500.00
Total         886,500.00
GBP
examples.note: The subtotal is bigger than the total. Anything reaching for the largest number on the page gets this wrong.
